newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada farm financial situation improving - survey.
newsitem.headline: Canada farm financial situation improving - survey.

text.p: The financial situation of Canadian farms improved steadily between 1993 and 1995 and probably in 1996 as well, according to a survey by Agriculture Canada.
The 1996 Farm Financial Survey, released on Friday, said assets rose to an average C$630,843 (US$460,515) per farm in 1995 from C$566,000 (US$413,180) in 1993.

"Generally prices have been very favorable in 1996 so I wouldn't expect any dramatic difference from the results of this survey," David Culver, Agriculture Canada analyst, told reporters at a news conference.

According to the survey, which was based on farm balance sheet results as of December 31, 1995, gross capital investment in Canadian agriculture increased to C$8.5 billion (US$6.2 billion) in 1995, or an average C$33,861 (US$24,719) per farm, up from C$31,650 (US$23,105) in 1993.

The largest growth in asset values and net worth over the two years of the survey took place in Canada's Atlantic region and especially in the province of Prince Edward Island. Strong growth was also recorded in Saskatchewan and Quebec.
The average net cash farm income (before depreciation) was higher in 1995 for all farm types except beef and poultry, and in all farm regions except Manitoba, the survey said.
At the national level, net cash farm income reached an average C$26,396 (US$19,269) per farm in 1995, up from C$23,435 (US$17,108) in 1993.
"Large increases in revenues from sales of grains and oilseeds, hogs and potatoes were primarily responsible for the rise in net farm cash income," the survey said.
Off-farm income rose to an average C$24,103 (US$17,595) in 1995 from C$22,322 (US$16,295) in 1993.
Average debt per farm rose between 1993 and 1995 after a decline between 1991 and 1993. But debt as a percentage of assets declined in all provinces except Ontario and British Columbia.
